findings.desc: [codex-host-2, verified] --resume breaks a LIVE lock and can let two writers corrupt the ledger. The resume-only stale-lock break deletes any existing .batch-ledger.lock WITHOUT checking whether the holder process is still alive. Scenario: driver A is still running and holds the lock; driver B starts --resume, removes A's LIVE lock, acquires its own, skips A's already-written records, and appends the rest while A keeps appending too -> duplicate/corrupt ledger, and B may exit 0 before A appends later duplicates. Fix: the stale-lock break must check the holder PID liveness (read the lock's holder.json/pid; break ONLY if the process is dead). A live holder means a genuine concurrent driver -> precondition_failed, not a break.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in aad1db055. acquireLock() now stamps LOCK_DIR/holder.json{pid}; the resume-only lock break probes holder liveness (process.kill(pid,0)) and breaks ONLY a dead/missing holder — a LIVE holder records precondition_failed to the blocked-ledger and exits 3. selfcheck-m3 (H) confirms: --resume refuses to break a live lock (exit 3) and breaks it only after the holder dies (discriminating).

findings.desc: [codex-host-2, verified] Truncated-tail repair can wrongly drop a VALID final record. repairTruncatedTail truncates the trailing line, but a genuinely complete final record whose line simply lacks a trailing newline (valid JSON, no newline at EOF) would be dropped -> that iterationId becomes a GAP on resume (or a spurious re-run/dup). Fix: only drop the trailing segment if it does NOT parse as valid JSON (genuinely incomplete); if the last line parses cleanly, KEEP it as a complete record. Distinguish 'valid record, no trailing newline' (keep) from 'truncated partial write' (drop).
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in aad1db055. repairTruncatedTail now parses the un-terminated tail in BOTH branches (shared isCompleteLedgerRecordLine helper): a complete final record missing only its trailing newline is PRESERVED verbatim; only a genuinely-incomplete partial write is dropped. selfcheck-m3 (G) confirms replay/small/4 preserved -> no gap.

findings.desc: repairTruncatedTail (run-batch.mjs:182-220) unconditionally drops everything after the last newline when the ledger file does not end with \n, even when that trailing fragment is a COMPLETE, valid, parseable JSON record — contradicting its own documented invariant ("Every COMPLETE prior record is preserved verbatim", line 178; "All well-formed prior lines are honored", line 129-131). Reproduced: a ledger of rec1\n + rec2 (rec2 complete JSON, only missing the trailing newline) has rec2 silently deleted by repairTruncatedTail, so its already-completed iteration is silently discarded and re-run on resume. The single-line branch (lastNl < 0, lines 197-209) DOES check JSON.parse before dropping and preserves a parseable lone line, but the multi-line branch (lines 210-219) drops unconditionally without ever checking whether the trailing fragment parses — an inconsistent/incomplete repair that can discard real evidence though it does not create a duplicate.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in aad1db055 (same fix as F-002 — the truncated-tail bug). Both single-line and multi-line branches now check parseability before dropping; a valid complete final record without a trailing newline is never dropped into a gap. selfcheck-m3 (G) covers it.

findings.desc: CHK-002 and understanding.json explicitly specify the H3 mid-iteration kill mechanism as the pre-existing POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT hook (a caught throw AFTER workspace write producing a verify_crash STOP record) — understanding.json facts: the mid-iteration crash hook already exists: POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT; unknowns: whether a mid-append truncated line actually occurs under POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT, resolved by the probe run. The delivered resume-probe.mjs (killA/killB, lines 339-345) and selfcheck-m3.mjs (killResumeTrial A/B, lines 350-352) never exercise POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT at all: both scored kills use the NEW POS_CRASH_BEFORE_APPEND_AT hard-exit hook at two different indices, i.e. the SAME mechanism twice, not two distinct injection points. The only real SIGKILL trial (externalSigkillTrial) is explicitly informational/non-gating and excluded from the dupTotal/gapTotal pass-fail computation. As a result resume behavior when the interrupted iteration already produced a caught stop record (rather than being genuinely recordless) is never asserted anywhere in M3 tests — the storys own pre-DEV automated advisory review (review.json unresolved_unknowns) flagged this exact unknown, and the implementation routed around it with a different mechanism rather than resolving it.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in aad1db055. resume-probe.mjs killC uses POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT (a caught fault -> a recorded verify_crash STOP at replay/small/3), then resume SKIPS that already-recorded stop (stoppedRecordPreserved:true, not re-run into a proof); selfcheck-m3 sub-check F asserts the stop-record-resume path. The POS_FAIL_APPEND_AT mechanism is now exercised.

findings.desc: [codex-host-2 re-check, verified] --resume can STILL break a LIVE lock during the mkdir-to-holder stamp race. The F-001 fix stamps holder.json{pid} AFTER mkdirSync(LOCK_DIR), and the resume break treats a missing/malformed holder.json as stale. Scenario: driver A wins mkdirSync(LOCK_DIR) but has not yet completed writeFileSync(holder.json); driver B (--resume) sees LOCK_DIR with no/half-written holder.json, judges it stale, removes it, acquires its own, and both append concurrently -> corruption. The holder stamp is not an atomic part of lock acquisition. Fix: treat a MISSING/malformed/unparseable holder.json as LIVE (conservative — do NOT break; precondition_failed); break ONLY when holder.json exists with a parseable pid that is DEAD. A genuinely-orphaned prior run wrote holder.json before crashing so it stays breakable; only a crash in the tiny mkdir->stamp window is not auto-broken (safe: requires manual cleanup, never corruption). Add a selfcheck sub-check: a lock dir with NO holder.json is NOT broken by --resume.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 1dad360a8: evaluateLockForBreak() conservative rule — a missing/unreadable/malformed/uncertain holder is treated as LIVE (not breakable); only a positively-proven-DEAD pid (ESRCH) is broken. Holder stamp near-atomic (temp-write+renameSync). Closes the mkdir->stamp acquire-window race. selfcheck-m3 sub-check I.

findings.desc: Independently corroborating open F-005 (codex-host-2): isLockHolderAlive() (run-batch.mjs:325-341) treats a missing/unparseable holder.json as STALE (line 331: "missing / unreadable / malformed holder -> treat as stale"), and acquireLock() (run-batch.mjs) writes HOLDER_PATH only AFTER mkdirSync(LOCK_DIR) succeeds -- there is a real window between mkdir winning the lock and the holder.json write landing where a concurrent --resume run would see LOCK_DIR present with no holder.json, judge it stale, and rmSync it out from under a live driver, letting two writers append concurrently (ledger corruption). Confirmed by direct code read; the fix (conservative direction: missing/malformed holder.json should be treated as LIVE/unbreakable, not stale) is not yet present in this diff. This is the same root cause as F-005 and blocks a clean pass on the F-001 area of this round.

multi-resumer-toctou: run-batch.mjs:749-787 evaluateLockForBreak() computes a breakable/proven-dead verdict from a one-time read of holder.json, but the subsequent rmSync(LOCK_DIR) at line 780 is unconditional on path and never re-validates that the lock dir still holds the SAME dead-pid holder it evaluated. Concrete interleaving: two concurrent --resume drivers A and B both see the same genuinely-dead-pid holder.json and both compute {breakable:true}. A calls rmSync(LOCK_DIR) then acquireLock() -> mkdirSync succeeds -> A now owns a freshly-live lock (about to stamp its own holder.json). B, acting on its stale verdict computed before A re-acquired, calls rmSync(LOCK_DIR) unconditionally -> deletes A live lock -> B then calls acquireLock() -> mkdirSync succeeds -> both A and B hold non-null releasers and both proceed to appendRecord() to the SAME batch-ledger.jsonl concurrently. This reintroduces the exact two-writer ledger-corruption scenario the F-001/F-005/F-006 fix chain was built to prevent -- it is just triggered by a THIRD racing resumer rather than the single acquire-window case this round closed. selfcheck-m3.mjs has no sub-check exercising two concurrent --resume invocations (checks H and I are both single-resumer only), so this gap is untested. A fix needs either a fencing/generation check (re-read+compare holder.json immediately before rmSync, or a rename-based conditional delete) so a stale verdict can never delete a lock dir that has since been re-acquired by someone else.

F-007 (cross-vendor host-2, Codex gpt-5.5 xhigh): Resume stale-lock break is TOCTOU. run-batch.mjs main() resume path (lines 749-791): evaluateLockForBreak() [CHECK] and rmSync(LOCK_DIR) [USE] are not atomic and rmSync targets the PATH not the instance judged. Interleaving: holder.json has a dead pid; resume drivers A+B both pass existsSync(LOCK_DIR) and both evaluateLockForBreak()->breakable:true; A rmSync(LOCK_DIR)+acquireLock() mkdir wins and stamps live pid A; B (acting on its already-computed stale verdict) rmSync(LOCK_DIR) DELETES A's now-LIVE lock, then acquireLock() mkdir wins for B too; both append to batch-ledger.jsonl -> the 'exactly one campaign writer' invariant is violated. Conservative missing-holder=LIVE does NOT protect A (B decided breakable before A's lock existed); the atomic holder rename does NOT help (B never re-reads the holder before rmSync). Fix: serialize the break critical-section (liveness check + destructive rmSync) with a dedicated break-mutex (mkdir-based) so no two breakers can interleave; the atomic mkdir(LOCK_DIR) stays the final arbiter (loser records precondition_failed). Add a selfcheck sub-check proving a break-in-progress blocks a second breaker (fail-closed) and that a freed break-mutex still lets a genuinely-stale lock be reclaimed.

F-009 (cross-vendor host-2, Codex gpt-5.5 xhigh): a FRESH (non-resume) driver can permanently poison a partial resume ledger via the break-to-reacquire window. Interleaving: prior run left batch-ledger.jsonl with K complete records + a stale lock (dead-pid holder). Resume driver R enters the break-mutex, proves the holder dead, rmSync(LOCK_DIR) (run-batch.mjs:829). Before R reaches acquireLock() (line ~872), a fresh non-resume driver F starts; F never checks BREAK_LOCK_DIR so its mkdir(LOCK_DIR) wins. R loses acquireLock() -> precondition_failed -> exits. F has resume=false so alreadyRecorded stays empty (line ~930): F re-runs EVERY iteration and appends replay/small/1..K that already exist. The end-of-run strict-multiset guard detects the duplicates and exits nonzero, BUT the campaign ledger file is already contaminated with duplicate records on disk, and a later --resume cannot repair a duplicate ledger (the multiset guard rejects it forever -> wedged evidence needing manual cleanup). This is NOT the two-live-writers bug (the mkdir lock still prevents simultaneous non-null releasers); it is that a fresh WINNER is allowed to write a dirty pre-existing ledger. Normally a stale lock protects the ledger from a fresh driver (fresh driver can't acquire), but resume recovery opens a window where a fresh driver can. Fix: fresh (non-resume) mode should FAIL CLOSED (precondition_failed) if batch-ledger.jsonl already exists and is non-empty, BEFORE any append — so a fresh driver never contaminates an existing campaign ledger. Codex also confirmed: no remaining two-non-null-releaser path; the break-mutex correctly must NOT auto-break (that would recreate the TOCTOU one level up); sub-check J.1/J.2 genuinely exercises the regression path and cleans its sandbox.

run-batch.mjs:829 -- the F-007/F-008 refactor dropped the prior explicit try/catch around rmSync(LOCK_DIR) during a genuine stale-lock break (present in commit 1dad360a8: try { rmSync(LOCK_DIR,...) } catch (e) { fatal(...) }). Now rmSync(LOCK_DIR) at line 829 is bare inside the outer try (814-831): if it throws, only the finally releases the break-mutex, then the error propagates UNCAUGHT out of main(), crashing with a generic stack trace and default exit 1 instead of the previously-explicit tagged FATAL diagnostic at exit 2. Not a TOCTOU/correctness defect (mutex still releases cleanly, no orphan, no double-write) but a real loss of diagnostic quality for the rmSync-failure-during-break path.

Independently re-verified corroboration of already-open F-009 (codex, medium): this round's F-007/F-008 fix only serializes the break critical-section itself; it does NOT close the fresh-non-resume-driver race the reviewer brief's concern (1) asks about. Concretely: after the break-mutex releases LOCK_DIR (run-batch.mjs finally at line 832-841) but BEFORE the resuming driver calls acquireLock() (line 872), a FRESH (--resume-less) driver can mkdirSync(LOCK_DIR) first and win it. That fresh driver has resume=false, so alreadyRecorded stays an empty Set (line 930) and it re-runs + appendFileSync-es EVERY expectedId, including ones already present in the pre-existing non-empty ledger from the interrupted prior run -- producing physical on-disk duplicate records before the end-of-run strict-multiset guard (runEndOfRunGuard) detects them and exits nonzero. The ledger is already contaminated by the time the guard fires (appendFileSync is irreversible), and a later --resume cannot repair a duplicate ledger (the multiset guard rejects it permanently). Confirmed still present against the current diff (4882fad0d only touches the break-mutex; main()'s fresh-vs-existing-ledger path at lines 930/949 is unchanged). This is NOT a duplicate of F-007/F-008 (no two-live-writers/mkdir-lock-race; the mkdir(LOCK_DIR) still resolves to exactly one winner) -- it is a fresh WINNER writing onto a dirty pre-existing ledger. Flagging so the quality-lane pass on THIS round's F-007/F-008 fix is not misread as covering F-009, which remains open and must be resolved before DONE.

concept-cleanup: selfcheck-m3.mjs top-of-file doc comment enumerates sub-checks (A)-(I) but omits a (J) entry for the newly added checkBreakMutexSerializes (F-007/F-008), even though it is fully implemented, registered, and called from main(). Non-blocking doc-completeness gap, not a functional residual -- the check itself runs correctly (verified green in this review: fresh dynamic run, all A-J including J.1/J.2 passed, selfcheck-m3 PASS).

F-013 (cross-vendor host-2, Codex gpt-5.5 xhigh): the F-009 fresh-mode non-empty-ledger guard FAILS OPEN on an unreadable existing ledger. run-batch.mjs ~lines 923-928: existingLedgerNonEmpty = existsSync(LEDGER_PATH) && readFileSync(LEDGER_PATH,'utf8').trim() !== '', with catch { existingLedgerNonEmpty = false }. If batch-ledger.jsonl EXISTS and is non-empty but readFileSync THROWS (e.g. a write-only file chmod 0200, or EACCES), the catch classifies it as EMPTY, so a fresh (non-resume) driver proceeds and appends new records onto the existing ledger -> on-disk duplicates (end-guard exits nonzero but the ledger is already poisoned). Since the catch only runs when existsSync already returned true (short-circuit &&), a read failure means the ledger EXISTS but is unverifiable — for a fail-CLOSED integrity instrument the correct posture is to REFUSE (treat as non-empty), not proceed. Fix: in the catch set existingLedgerNonEmpty = true (fail closed) so an existing-but-unreadable ledger blocks a fresh run. Codex also CONFIRMED convergence on everything else: no interleaving (two-fresh / fresh-vs-resume / resume-vs-resume) yields two non-null campaign writers; F-010 releases the break-mutex in finally before both the breakError exit-2 and precondReason exit-3 paths (mutually exclusive); sub-check K is genuine vs the prior regression and hermetic.

CHK-001:adversarial and CHK-003:adversarial evidence notes claim the fresh-mode non-empty-ledger fail-closed guard makes the campaign ledger un-poisonable ("the exactly one campaign writer, never a poisoned ledger invariant holds"; sub-check K "proves" this), but this overstates the actual coverage: run-batch.mjs:922-928 -- existingLedgerNonEmpty = existsSync(LEDGER_PATH) && readFileSync(LEDGER_PATH,"utf8").trim() !== "", with catch { existingLedgerNonEmpty = false } -- FAILS OPEN when the ledger exists, is non-empty, but readFileSync THROWS (e.g. EACCES/unreadable). The catch runs only after existsSync already returned true, so a read failure on an existing ledger is misclassified as EMPTY and a fresh driver proceeds to append onto it, producing on-disk duplicates. selfcheck-m3.mjs sub-check K (checkFreshRefusesNonemptyLedger) only seeds a READABLE non-empty ledger and never exercises the unreadable-but-non-empty branch, so this fail-open path is untested. This exact gap is already independently filed and open as B-f511:F-013 (medium/adversarial, cross-vendor Codex, this same review round, reviewRunId RR-026, evidenceState verified) with a concrete fix (set existingLedgerNonEmpty = true in the catch to fail closed). Flagging from the test-coverage lane because the CHK-001/CHK-003 adversarial verificationEvidence notes assert a universal fail-closed guarantee that the current evidence (sub-check K) does not actually establish -- the claim needs either a fix + a dedicated sub-check for the unreadable-ledger path, or the evidence note must be narrowed to not claim the invariant holds unconditionally.

CHK-003:adversarial verificationEvidence note for this round claims: "F-010 restores the explicit [resume] could-not-break-stale-lock exit 2 diagnostic; every direction fails loudly on regression." This overstates coverage: F-010 (the breakError capture at run-batch.mjs:819/838-842 and the restored FATAL exit-2 diagnostic at run-batch.mjs:860-865) has ZERO dedicated test coverage in selfcheck-m3.mjs -- confirmed by exhaustive grep across the full file history (grep -n "F-010" and grep -n "could not break\\|breakError" both return no matches in any commit that touches selfcheck-m3.mjs, including the current HEAD). None of sub-checks A-K ever forces rmSync(LOCK_DIR) to throw during a genuine stale-lock break (e.g. by making LOCK_DIR unremovable/permission-denied mid-break), so the breakError branch and its exit-2 FATAL path are exercised by neither a positive nor a negative assertion -- they are silently untested production code. Sub-check K (F-009/F-011) and sub-check J (F-007/F-008) are unrelated to this path. This is consistent with prior test-coverage review passes (RP-002/RP-004/RP-006) which also never claimed F-010 mapped to a sub-check. Not blocking DONE by itself (F-010 is a low-severity diagnostic-quality fix, not a correctness defect, per the original F-010 finding text), but the verificationEvidence note text should not claim blanket "every direction fails loudly on regression" coverage while this specific diagnostic path remains untested -- either add a dedicated sub-check that forces the rmSync(LOCK_DIR) break to fail (e.g. chmod the break target or replace it with a non-empty/busy directory) and asserts exit 2 with the FATAL message, or correct the evidence note to scope the claim to only the tested directions.

Independently reproduced/corroborating open F-013 (Codex host-2): the F-009/F-011 fresh-mode non-empty-ledger guard (run-batch.mjs:922-928) fails OPEN on an unreadable existing ledger. existingLedgerNonEmpty = existsSync(LEDGER_PATH) && readFileSync(LEDGER_PATH,"utf8").trim() !== "", wrapped in try { } catch { existingLedgerNonEmpty = false }. Reproduced directly: chmod 000 a non-empty batch-ledger.jsonl, then existsSync(...) returns true but readFileSync(...) throws EACCES; the catch sets existingLedgerNonEmpty=false, so a fresh (non-resume) driver treats an EXISTING non-empty ledger it could not read as EMPTY and proceeds to append every expected iterationId onto it, producing on-disk duplicates the end-of-run guard can detect only AFTER the ledger is already poisoned (appendFileSync is irreversible) -- contradicting the guards own fail-closed design intent stated in the surrounding comment (a FRESH driver must never append onto a non-empty pre-existing campaign ledger). Fix direction: in the catch, set existingLedgerNonEmpty = true (fail closed on any read failure of an existing file), mirroring the conservative missing-holder=LIVE precedent already used for the lock-break decision (F-005/F-006).

quality-cleanup: selfcheck-m3.mjs fail() (line 141-144) calls process.exit(1), which per Node.js semantics skips pending finally blocks. Every sub-check (including the new L/M added in 98ee3e0db) wraps its body in try { ... } finally { rmSync(sandbox, { recursive: true, force: true }); } -- but that cleanup is SKIPPED whenever fail() fires inside the try (i.e. exactly on a genuine regression). Reproduced directly: reverting the F-013/F-016 catch-branch fix (existingLedgerNonEmpty=false) makes sub-check L call fail(), and the sandbox dir pos-selfcheck-m3-L-fresh-fails-closed-on-unreadable-ledger-* is left on disk under os.tmpdir() (not cleaned). Same reproduced for M (removing the F-010 try/catch makes M call fail() and leaks its sandbox + a spawnDeadPid-derived tmp dir). This is a pre-existing property of the shared fail() helper (not introduced by this diff, and other sub-checks A-K share it), so it does not affect the happy-path hermeticity claimed for the shipped code (a clean PASS run leaves no pos-selfcheck-m3-* leak -- verified directly). But it means the two NEW sub-checks this round are only hermetic on PASS, not on FAIL, which weakens exactly the regression-detection runs where cleanup matters most for CI/local disk hygiene. Suggested fix: replace process.exit(1) in fail() with throw new Error(msg) and let main()'s existing .catch(e) handler print + exit 1, so try/finally blocks run normally on failure.

test-coverage-gap: selfcheck-m3.mjs checkResumeBreakFailureDiagnostic (sub-check M, lines 1095-1147) asserts exit code 2, the diagnostic string, no orphaned break-mutex, and campaign-ledger untouched -- but never asserts that .batch-ledger.lock (LOCK_DIR) itself is still present/intact on disk after the forced break failure. Code inspection confirms POS_FAIL_LOCK_BREAK throws strictly BEFORE the real rmSync(LOCK_DIR, ...) call (run-batch.mjs:842-845), so LOCK_DIR necessarily survives today, but sub-check M does not verify this directly -- an implementer could accidentally reorder the fault-injection check to AFTER a partial rmSync side effect (or otherwise change the surrounding logic) without M catching it, since M only checks the break-mutex and campaign ledger, not the stale-lock directory whose survival is the operationally-important fact for a manual-cleanup recovery story. Suggested addition: after the breakRun assertion, add existsSync(lockDirPath(sandbox)) && existsSync(holderPath(sandbox)) checks (mirroring the pattern already used in sub-checks H/I) to make the LOCK_DIR-survives invariant explicit and regression-tested.
